thesis: The bear carries the present cash-conversion objection: ad demand growth has not overcome near-total capex absorption and weaker earnings. Identified charges qualify recurrence but cannot establish infrastructure returns. Neutral retains the verified monetisation engine and avoids assuming costs persist unchanged or that the recovery has already occurred.
strongest_counterexample: Impressions grew14% and price/ad12%, supporting revenue growth28%; identified $2.4bn legal and $1.18bn severance charges make the reported margin decline an incomplete recurring comparison.
invalidation_conditions: A subsequent comparable quarter reports FCF above the observed $784m and positive normalised operating-income growth after a complete cost bridge, reversing the current conversion objection.
Ad impressions growth and pricing growth both at or below zero in a comparable quarter would defeat the retained demand-engine counterweight.
evidence_gaps: Infrastructure returns, repeatable post-capex cash and lease-inclusive obligations.
decisive_factors: Known charges do not remove capex absorption; slowing MACD after a sharp rally.
